atoms.text: This guide configures the Tidewater Query Engine to read raw CSV access logs and write query results using a single AWS account. The engine runs under an IAM role named TidewaterQueryRole in account 111122223333. The input data is stored under the prefix raw-logs/ in the bucket acme-analytics-logs, which is also owned by account 111122223333. Query output is written to the prefix query-results/ in the same bucket. Attach an identity-based policy to TidewaterQueryRole that allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket, restricted to those two prefixes with an s3:prefix condition. The same policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-logs/raw-logs/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-logs/query-results/*. Because the role and the bucket belong to the same account, this identity-based policy is sufficient to grant access, and the bucket policy is not changed. Confirm that no existing bucket policy statement contains an explicit Deny that matches the role. Run a test query that scans one day of logs and verify that a result object appears under query-results/.

This guide configures the Tidewater Query Engine to read raw CSV access logs and write query results across two AWS accounts. The engine runs under an IAM role named TidewaterQueryRole in account 111122223333. The input data is stored under the prefix raw-logs/ in the bucket acme-analytics-logs, which is owned by a different account, 444455556666. Query output is written to the prefix query-results/ in that same bucket. The bucket owner adds a statement to the bucket policy whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/TidewaterQueryRole. That statement allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket, restricted to the two prefixes with an s3:prefix condition, s3:GetObject on raw-logs/*, and s3:PutObject on query-results/*. Because the bucket belongs to another account, the bucket policy carries the grant, and the role's own account must also allow these actions in an identity-based policy. Set the bucket's Object Ownership to Bucket owner enforced so that result objects written by the role are owned by account 444455556666. Run a test query that scans one day of logs and verify that a result object appears under query-results/.

This guide gives the Marlow Batch Loader access to a landing bucket so it can read Parquet files and write compacted output within one account. The loader runs under an IAM role named MarlowLoaderRole in account 111122223333. Raw Parquet files arrive under the prefix landing/ in the bucket acme-ingest-landing, which is owned by the same account. The loader compacts them into larger files and writes them under the prefix compacted/ in that bucket. Create an identity-based policy for MarlowLoaderRole that allows s3:GetObject on landing/* and s3:PutObject on compacted/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket itself, and s3:DeleteObject on landing/* only if the job removes source files after compaction. The role and the bucket share an account, so the identity-based policy alone grants access and the bucket policy is left unchanged. Check the bucket's Block Public Access settings, which should remain enabled. Start a loader job against a single partition and confirm that the compacted file is created and its size matches the expected row count.

This guide gives the Marlow Batch Loader access to a landing bucket so it can read Parquet files and write compacted output across accounts. The loader runs under an IAM role named MarlowLoaderRole in account 111122223333. Raw Parquet files arrive under the prefix landing/ in the bucket acme-ingest-landing, which is owned by a different account, 444455556666. The loader compacts them into larger files and writes them under the prefix compacted/ in that bucket. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/MarlowLoaderRole as the Principal. The statement allows s3:GetObject on landing/* and s3:PutObject on compacted/*, plus s3:ListBucket on the bucket itself. It also allows s3:DeleteObject on landing/* only if the job removes source files after compaction. Because the bucket is in another account, the bucket policy carries the grant, and the role's account must also permit the same actions in an identity-based policy. Keep the bucket's Block Public Access settings enabled. Start a loader job against a single partition and confirm that the compacted file is created and its size matches the expected row count.

This guide covers access for the Corvid Stream Collector, which reads buffered event files and writes rejected records to a dead-letter location in one account. The collector runs under an IAM role named CorvidCollectorRole in account 111122223333. Buffered JSON event files are stored under the prefix buffer/ in the bucket acme-events-store, owned by the same account. Records that fail schema validation are written under the prefix dead-letter/ in that bucket. Attach an identity-based policy to CorvidCollectorRole that allows s3:GetObject on buffer/* and s3:PutObject on dead-letter/*. Include s3:ListBucket on the bucket with an s3:prefix condition limited to buffer/. Since the role and the bucket are in the same account, no change to the bucket policy is required and none is made. Review the role's permissions boundary, if one exists, to ensure it does not exclude these actions. Send a malformed test event and confirm that a corresponding object appears under dead-letter/ within one flush interval.

The statement allows s3:GetObject on buffer/* and s3:PutObject on dead-letter/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with an s3:prefix condition limited to buffer/. Because the bucket is in another account, the bucket policy carries the grant, and the role's own account must also allow these actions through an identity-based policy. Review the role's permissions boundary, if one exists, to ensure it does not exclude these actions. This guide grants the Helix Report Scheduler access to clickstream data and a report destination inside one account. The scheduler runs under an IAM role named HelixSchedulerRole in account 111122223333. Hourly clickstream files are read from the prefix clickstream/ in the bucket acme-web-analytics, which is owned by the same account. The scheduler aggregates them and writes daily summary files to the prefix reports/daily/ in that bucket. Define an identity-based policy on HelixSchedulerRole that allows s3:GetObject on clickstream/* and s3:PutObject on reports/daily/*. Add s3:ListBucket for the bucket, scoped to the clickstream/ and reports/daily/ prefixes. The role and the bucket are in the same account, so the identity-based policy is the only place the grant is made and the bucket policy remains as it was. Verify that the scheduler's trust policy allows the Helix service to assume the role. Trigger a manual run for yesterday's date and confirm that a summary file is created under reports/daily/.

This guide grants the Helix Report Scheduler access to clickstream data and a report destination across two accounts. The scheduler runs under an IAM role named HelixSchedulerRole in account 111122223333. Hourly clickstream files are read from the prefix clickstream/ in the bucket acme-web-analytics, which is owned by a different account, 444455556666. The scheduler aggregates them and writes daily summary files to the prefix reports/daily/ in that bucket. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names the account ID 111122223333 as the Principal, with a condition on aws:PrincipalArn matching the HelixSchedulerRole ARN. The statement allows s3:GetObject on clickstream/* and s3:PutObject on reports/daily/*, plus s3:ListBucket scoped to both prefixes. Because the bucket is in another account, the bucket policy carries the grant, and the role's account must also allow these actions in an identity-based policy. Verify that the scheduler's trust policy allows the Helix service to assume the role. Trigger a manual run for yesterday's date and confirm that a summary file is created under reports/daily/.

This guide sets up the Quillon Feature Builder to read event data and write feature snapshots using one account. The builder runs under an IAM role named QuillonBuilderRole in account 111122223333. Event files in Avro format are read from the prefix events/ in the bucket acme-ml-data, which is owned by the same account. Each run writes a versioned snapshot under the prefix features/snapshots/ in that bucket. Attach an identity-based policy to QuillonBuilderRole that allows s3:GetObject on events/* and s3:PutObject on features/snapshots/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket and s3:GetBucketLocation so the builder can resolve the bucket's region. The bucket and the role share an account, so the identity-based policy alone is sufficient and the bucket policy is not edited. If the bucket uses SSE-KMS, the role also needs permission to use that key. Run the builder for a one-hour window and confirm that a snapshot object with the expected version suffix is written.

This guide sets up the Quillon Feature Builder to read event data and write feature snapshots across two accounts. The builder runs under an IAM role named QuillonBuilderRole in account 111122223333. Event files in Avro format are read from the prefix events/ in the bucket acme-ml-data, which is owned by a different account, 444455556666. Each run writes a versioned snapshot under the prefix features/snapshots/ in that bucket. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/QuillonBuilderRole as the Principal. The statement allows s3:GetObject on events/*, s3:PutObject on features/snapshots/*, s3:ListBucket, and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket. Because the bucket is in another account, the bucket policy carries the grant, and the role's account must also allow these actions through an identity-based policy. If the bucket uses SSE-KMS, the key policy must also permit the role. Run the builder for a one-hour window and confirm that a snapshot object with the expected version suffix is written.

This guide configures the Brannock Log Compactor to read small JSON log files and write partitioned ORC output within a single account. The compactor runs under an IAM role named BrannockCompactorRole in account 111122223333. Source files are read from the prefix app-logs/incoming/ in the bucket acme-observability, which is owned by the same account. Output is written under the prefix app-logs/orc/ with Hive-style date partitions. Attach an identity-based policy to BrannockCompactorRole that allows s3:GetObject on app-logs/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on app-logs/orc/*. Add s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads so that large output files can be uploaded in parts and cleaned up on failure. The role and the bucket are in the same account, so the identity-based policy grants access and the bucket policy is unchanged. Confirm that no bucketlifecycle rule expires the incoming prefix before the compactor has read it. Run the compactor on one hour of logs and check that the output partitions are created.

This guide configures the Brannock Log Compactor to read small JSON log files and write partitioned ORC output across two accounts. The compactor runs under an IAM role named BrannockCompactorRole in account 111122223333. Source files are read from the prefix app-logs/incoming/ in the bucket acme-observability, which is owned by a different account, 444455556666. Output is written under the prefix app-logs/orc/ with Hive-style date partitions. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement with the Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/BrannockCompactorRole. The statement allows s3:GetObject on app-logs/incoming/*, s3:PutObject on app-logs/orc/*, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads so large output files can be uploaded in parts. Because the bucket is in another account, the bucket policy carries the grant, and the role's account must also allow these actions in an identity-based policy. Confirm that no bucket lifecycle rule expires the incoming prefix before the compactor has read it. Run the compactor on one hour of logs and check that the output partitions are created.

This guide gives the Pelham Data Validator access to daily file drops and a location for validation reports in one account. The validator runs under an IAM role named PelhamValidatorRole in account 111122223333. Partner files are read from the prefix drops/YYYY-MM-DD/ in the bucket acme-partner-intake, owned by the same account. For each file, the validator writes a JSON report under the prefix validation/reports/ in that bucket. Create an identity-based policy for PelhamValidatorRole that allows s3:GetObject on drops/* and s3:PutObject on validation/reports/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket, with an s3:prefix condition that includes drops/. Because the role and bucket are in the same account, the grant is made only in the identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is not modified. Enable S3 versioning on the bucket if reports must be retained across reruns. Place a sample file in today's drop folder and confirm that a matching report appears under validation/reports/ after the validator's next scheduled run.

This guide gives the Pelham Data Validator access to daily file drops and a location for validation reports across two accounts. The validator runs under an IAM role named PelhamValidatorRole in account 111122223333. Partner files are read from the prefix drops/YYYY-MM-DD/ in the bucket acme-partner-intake, owned by a different account, 444455556666. For each file, the validator writes a JSON report under the prefix validation/reports/ in that bucket. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming the account ID 111122223333 as the Principal, with an aws:PrincipalArn condition matching PelhamValidatorRole. The statement allows s3:GetObject on drops/*, s3:PutObject on validation/reports/*, and s3:ListBucket with an s3:prefix condition that includes drops/. Because the bucket is in another account, the bucket policy carries the grant, and the role's account must also permit these actions in an identity-based policy. Enable S3 versioning on the bucket if reports must be retained across reruns. Place a sample file in today's drop folder and confirm that a matching report appears under validation/reports/ after the validator's next scheduled run.

This guide allows the Odell Geo Enrichment job to read GPS ping files and write enriched output within one account. The job runs under an IAM role named OdellEnrichRole in account 111122223333. Compressed GPS ping files are read from the prefix pings/raw/ in the bucket acme-location-data, which is owned by the same account. The job joins them with reference data and writes enriched files under the prefix pings/enriched/ in that bucket. Attach an identity-based policy to OdellEnrichRole that allows s3:GetObject on pings/raw/* and s3:PutObject on pings/enriched/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket, restricted by an s3:prefix condition to pings/. The role and the bucket share an account, so no bucket policy statement is added and the existing bucket policy is left in place. Verify that the job's task execution settings reference OdellEnrichRole rather than a default role. Run the job for a small bounding box and confirm that enriched files are created with the same row counts as the input.
